justification: Standard: source-control visibility, Linux dependency selection, and bootstrap-documentation accuracy across the whole branch — not production data or a served route. A silently-shadowed migration or fix script absent from a fresh clone is an operational gap, not a data-corruption risk, so Minor would understate it and Critical overstates it.

deferred_out_of_this_commit.why: This branch's earlier commits (302ac3ab) staged ~81 previously-gitignore-shadowed scripts/migration files. Pushing tripped two separate content gates on 55 of them (11 overlapping): scripts/lint_hardcoded_zone_codes.py (DQ-30, hardcoded NSW zone-code lists) and scripts/qa_gate.py's DB guard (queries against regulatory_provisions without an is_current/v2_is_actionable filter within +/-10 lines) plus 10 adversarial null-safety findings. These are historical one-off diagnostic/fix scripts (Jan-Feb 2026, heritage/DCP page-repair work), not live-serving code, so the 'don't serve stale data to a user' rationale behind the DB guard may not fit them the way it fits services/ or API routes -- but that is a judgment call this session should not make unilaterally for 44 files it did not author. Removed from tracking via `git rm --cached` rather than silently left ignored, so `git status` shows them as ordinary untracked files (visible, not hidden) pending that review. Still absent from a fresh clone.

falsifiable_check.command: git check-ignore -q frontend-nextjs/lib/schemas/extracted-rule.ts; test $? -eq 1; git check-ignore -q scripts/definitions/import_definitions.py; test $? -eq 1; git ls-files scripts/definitions/check_sepp_housing.py | grep -q . && echo STILL_TRACKED_SHOULD_BE_DEFERRED
falsifiable_check.fails_when: Either genuinely-fixed file is still ignored (proving it would be absent from a fresh clone), or a deferred file is still tracked despite tripping the zone-code/DB-guard gates.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Before this branch: frontend-nextjs/lib/schemas/extracted-rule.ts was killed by a bare `schemas/` rule; scripts/definitions/, scripts/diagnostics/, scripts/enrichment/, scripts/fixes/, scripts/procedural/, scripts/verification/, scripts/migrations/, scripts/sql/ and root migrations/ were killed by basename globs (check_*.py, fix_*.py, create_*.py, *.sql, ...) that match at any depth, one level past where an earlier fix's `!scripts/*.py`-style negations reached.
falsifiable_check.observed_green: git check-ignore -q now exits 1 (not ignored) for the 33 files actually committed on this branch; the 55 files that trip the zone-code lint or the DB guard were deliberately un-staged via `git rm --cached` after discovery, so they remain absent from a fresh clone pending a dedicated review rather than being force-committed past a data-integrity gate.

functions.name: load_definitions_from_json
functions.input: json_path (pathlib.Path) to a definitions JSON file
functions.output: list[dict] of definitions, or [] if the path does not exist
functions.if_none: Missing file prints a [SKIP] line and returns an empty list rather than raising; this script itself (and the scripts/definitions/extracted/*.json it reads) now exist in Git for a fresh clone to run at all, which is the defect this change fixes.

pre_impl.existing_data: None. This change only affects Git tracking and documentation text; it does not read or write database rows.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: An earlier fix's `!scripts/*.py` / `!scripts/*.sql` negations were assumed to cover the whole scripts/ tree; gitignore's `*` does not cross `/`, so they only reached files directly under scripts/, not scripts/<subdir>/.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Forward-only source-control repair. Existing working copies are unaffected; fresh clones now receive the previously-hidden files that survived the zone-code/DB-guard review filter.
pre_impl.external_source_error: N/A -- no external service called by the .gitignore/tracking change. The runbook's DeepSeek Harness install command and GitHub URL were verified via WebFetch against github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness directly (not secondary blog sources) before being left unchanged; the Node-version claim from third-party guides could NOT be confirmed against that primary source, so the runbook now says so explicitly rather than asserting an unverified number.
pre_impl.frontend_type: N/A -- no frontend route or type touched.

break_it.scenario: A fresh Linux clone runs a DCP definitions or heritage-tagging fix script referenced in project docs (e.g. scripts/definitions/import_definitions.py)
break_it.what_happens: python: can't open file -- the script does not exist, because it was never committed.
break_it.how: .gitignore now re-includes *.py/*.sql/*.sh/*.mjs/*.js/*.bat at any depth under scripts/ (`!scripts/**/*.py` etc.), not just one level deep; the 33 files that pass both content gates are now tracked. The remaining 55 are deliberately still absent -- see deferred_out_of_this_commit -- so this failure mode persists FOR THOSE SPECIFIC FILES until that review happens, by design rather than by accident.
break_it.repro: git ls-files scripts/definitions/ scripts/diagnostics/ | wc -l  # was 0 for these two dirs before this branch

break_it.scenario: An operator follows docs/LINUX_DEEPSEEK_BOOTSTRAP_RUNBOOK.md step 4 exactly as written before this change
break_it.what_happens: `git switch fix/linux-repro-gitignore-holes` fails -- that branch was never pushed to origin at the time the runbook was first drafted, so the clone had no such ref, and the runbook's own 'staged but not yet committed' warning was already stale.
break_it.how: Runbook now states the repair is on this branch/main as applicable (no unresolved branch switch) and gives a git check-ignore command to verify the repair is present.

break_it.scenario: Operator installs only the Node version this repo's SETUP.md specifies (20 LTS) and assumes it also satisfies DeepSeek Harness
break_it.what_happens: `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web` may fail to start if DSH's actual minimum (third-party guides claim ^22.19.0/>=24.x, unconfirmed by the DSH README itself) is higher than 20 LTS.
break_it.how: Runbook section 5 flags the version as unconfirmed from DSH's primary source, tells the operator to read the actual startup error rather than trust a number, and to use nvm for a second Node version rather than replacing the repo's pinned one.
break_it.repro: n/a -- documentation caveat, not a code path

break_it.scenario: This commit force-tracks a script whose regulatory_provisions query lacks an is_current/v2_is_actionable filter, and it is later run against production without the operator realizing it can act on superseded rows
break_it.what_happens: A heritage/DCP fix runs against stale or superseded provisions, producing a write based on outdated data.
break_it.how: All 44 files the DB guard (and the 10-finding adversarial null-safety scan) flagged were removed from tracking via git rm --cached rather than force-committed past the gate -- see deferred_out_of_this_commit.db_guard_and_adversarial_files.
break_it.repro: python scripts/qa_gate.py  # would list these under 'DB guard' if they were re-staged without a fix or an explicit reviewed exemption

post_merge.manual_verify: Yes -- a real fresh Linux clone + npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web run has not been performed (no Linux partition exists yet on the target machine); only Git visibility and primary-source documentation claims were verified from Windows. The 55 deferred files still need a human decision: mechanically add currency filters, add reviewed noqa suppressions, or leave excluded.
